Group Project I · Rapid Prototyping with AI · IE University

daba.

Book the empty seat. Now.

Full-price off-peak seats for independent boutique studios in Casablanca and Rabat. Newcomers only. No pack. The owner chooses.

Casablanca · Rabat · 13 October 2026 · Daba is Darija for “now”

Eight mats. Two regulars. One seat released to a newcomer, at full price.

Findings first. Don't introduce the team or the agenda; go straight to slide 2 within 10 seconds. If you say one thing here: "Daba means 'now' in Darija. Book the empty seat, now." The logo is the whole idea: eight mats, two regulars, one seat the owner releases to a newcomer at full price.

01 · The finding

+36 pts

Remove the pack, and newcomers book more than twice as often.

64% vs 28% · 50 real class-goers in Casablanca and Rabat · p = 0.011 · pass mark set before testing

Pause. Let the number sit. "We removed the pack, and bookings more than doubled: from 28% to 64%. This is Daba. And here's how we got there, including the three times we were wrong."

02 · We failed cheap and fast

Three cheap failures, each one logged

FAILURE 01

Wrong riskiest assumption

We bet on timing. A cross-review asked: how do you tell “wrong time” from “nobody wants that class”? We couldn’t.

→ Pivot: commitment is the risk

Cost: one PDF, a few WhatsApps

FAILURE 02

Offer designed without owners

Real users decided: four of five owners said “only if I choose the seats, and my regulars never see it.”

→ Pivot: newcomers only, full price, owner chooses

Cost: zero lines of code

FAILURE 03

Examples counted as evidence

Our card trials were illustrative, not real people. Your feedback caught it.

→ Fix: removed from 14 files; every recording checked against its report

Cost: a re-check, not a rebuild

02 · 13 decisions changed by evidence, each logged with its cause in pivot-log.md

daba.

"We didn't get here by being right. We got here by failing cheap and fast, three times. Failure one: wrong riskiest assumption. We believed the problem was timing; our first prototype was a concierge test, WhatsApp nudges by hand. Before a single token on code, a cross-review asked how we'd tell 'wrong time' from 'nobody wants that class'. We couldn't. Cost: one PDF. We pivoted to commitment. Failure two: we designed the offer without the owners. Then real users decided: four of five owners said 'only if I choose the seats and my regulars never see it'. Cost: zero lines of code. Failure three, the one we're proudest of fixing: we counted example card trials as evidence. You caught it. We kept simulated answers separate from real-user evidence, removed them from 14 files, and checked every recording against its report. Thirteen decisions changed because of evidence, not opinions."

03 · 6 owners, 7 goers, 1 founder · every recorded interview checked against its written report

daba.

Play one or two clips, not all four (watch the clock). "Our personas are grounded in behaviour, what people actually do and what stops them changing. Owners: a regular who's paid full price for months 'would ask questions'. Goers: Youssef's meeting was cancelled, he DMed a boxing studio, nobody replied for 40 minutes, he ate lunch at his desk. That's why we held instant confirmation constant in our test. Another goer has postponed her friend's reformer invitation for months: 'five classes upfront is a different story'. Two ways into the same job, a free window or a friend's invitation, and one barrier underneath: commitment before trust."

04 · The cheapest test that could prove us wrong

One risk. One test. One decision.

ONE RISK

Newcomers won’t book because a pack before trying feels like a bad bet.

Our riskiest assumption. If it’s false, the whole idea is false.

ONE TEST

A fake door: a booking page for a studio that doesn’t exist.

Built in one day. No backend, no payments. Sent over WhatsApp. Cost: 0 MAD.

ONE DECISION

Agreed before the first link went out.

≥ 30 pts and p < 0.05 → continue. Under 15 pts → the decline reasons pick the pivot: price, certainty or trust.

04 · The 300-dirham test

daba.

"Interviews tell you what people say. Real users decide by what they do. So we followed the rule: one risk, one test, one decision. One risk: our riskiest assumption. One test: the cheapest one that could prove us wrong, a fake door. A booking page for a studio that doesn't exist, built in one day, zero dirhams. One decision, agreed before testing: at least 30 points better with less than a 5% chance of luck, and if it failed, the reasons people gave would choose the pivot."

05 · Main reason given by each of the 27 people who didn’t reserve

daba.

"First question: did the pack cause the gap, or something else? People told us why they said no. 'Having to commit' came up zero times in the single-class version, and ten times in the pack version. Price and 'I prefer my gym' were about the same in both. We treat contradictions as signals: price is real, and we'll watch it. But the gap comes from the one thing we changed."

05 · Fisher’s exact test, Newcombe interval, Bayesian check with flat priors · ab-test-analysis.md

daba.

"Then we stress-tested it. 99%: the chance the single class really beats the pack. 8 to 57 points: the 95% range for the true gap. It's real, but we don't know exactly how big. 61%: the chance the true gap clears our own 30-point bar. Honest, not a slam dunk. And 3: our fragility index. If three people had answered differently, the test would have failed. So we're sure of the direction and humble about the size. That's exactly why our next step is a pilot, not a scale-up."

06 · How to read: higher = offers more of it · scores are team judgement

daba.

How to read it (say this first, 10 seconds): "This is a strategy canvas. Along the bottom, the seven things this market competes on. Each line is one option, and higher means it offers more of that thing. The dashed line, discounts, wins only on price. The dotted line, studios' own discovery packs, sits in the middle on everything. Our orange line does the opposite: low on price on purpose, high on the five things owners and newcomers told us they want." Then: "So why don't we just become another discount app? Because the whole market fights on price, and we don't. We score low on price on purpose: full price, always. And high on everything owners and newcomers actually asked for: no pack, a confirmed spot, price integrity, owner control, and knowing who's new. No competitor has that shape. That's our blue ocean."

06 · What AI can’t copy

Anyone can rebuild our app in a day.

01

Counter-positioning

Discount and credit apps can’t copy full price without breaking their own model.

02

A trust gate

“Newcomers only” needs member lists. Owners share those only with people they trust.

03

Relationships first

Six owners gave us their quiet classes and conditions. Two are open to a pilot.

04

A data flywheel

Every pilot week shows which seats turn newcomers into regulars. Copycats start at zero.

05

Local rhythm

Friday 12:30 empties for prayer and family lunch. That’s local knowledge, not code.

06

What not to build

Our test shows the pack, not price, drives the gap. Copycats guess and build discounts.

06 · Being first in Morocco is a window, not a moat

daba.

"Can AI copy our app? In a weekend; we built ours in a day. So our moat isn't the code. One: counter-positioning. Discount and credit apps make money selling cheaper access; copying 'full price, owner chooses' would break their own model. Two: a trust gate. 'Newcomers only' means checking studios' member lists, and owners hand those only to people they trust. NOVA's lesson. Three: relationships. Six owners already gave us their quiet classes and conditions, and two are open to a pilot. Four: a data flywheel. Every pilot week tells us which seats turn newcomers into regulars; a copycat starts at zero. Five: local rhythm. Karim's Friday 12:30 is empty because of prayer and family lunch; that's local knowledge, not code. And six, our favourite: we know what NOT to build. Our test shows the pack, not the price, drives the gap. A copycat guessing will build discounts. And being first in Morocco is a window, not a moat. We'll say that before you do."

07 · Owners A, C, D, E · 54 studios counted (likely an undercount) · 300 MAD a seat · size-of-the-prize.md

daba.

"You asked us to know the size of the prize, using data no one else has. Owners' quietest classes run about 30% full: 1,200 to 2,100 dirhams of empty seats per class, every week. Across Casablanca and Rabat, 450 to 680 thousand dirhams a week. One studio filling just two seats per quiet class gains about 18,000 dirhams a month. That's solopreneur scale first, and it grows with cities and formats like Hyrox."

07 · Will we waste time and tokens building it?

GO, narrowly.

Vibe-code from Session 16

  • Owner releases chosen seats
  • Offer shown to newcomers only
  • One class, no pack, full price
  • Confirmed within 1 minute
  • Studio marks attendance
  • New-vs-regular report

Not yet

  • Online payments
  • Credits or subscriptions
  • Discounts of any kind
  • A native app

We stop if

  • No owner releases a real seat
  • People reserve but don’t show up
  • Fewer than 30% come back at full price

Specs, requirements and agent rules are already in the repo. We build only what the next test needs: attendance and return can only be measured with something real people can book.

07 · build-decision.md · specs/roadmap.md

daba.

"You asked: will we waste time and tokens building it? No. We'll vibe-code only what the next test needs. Our specs and agent rules are written; a coding agent can start at Session 16. The two risks that could kill us, attendance and return, can only be measured with something real people can book, so building is now the cheapest way to learn. And we've written down what makes us stop. Would anyone invest? Not yet. They'd wait for one owner committing a real class, and newcomers who come back. That's exactly what the pilot measures."
